title: feat(plugin-security): a host can keep a platform baseline contribution at read, or decline it
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DXuamRUC67fx2TTYrFfyuSH)_

Fixes #33132

Clause-②: yes (widening) — `SecurityPlugin` accepts a new, opt-in option, `platformBaselineOverrides`, and the package exports two new types, `PlatformBaselineOverride` and `PlatformBaselineOverrides`. Omitted, every platform baseline contribution is admitted as contributed, as before.
Metadata-protocol: none

## Maintainer quick read

- What changes: a host can now say, in its `SecurityPlugin` configuration, "members keep reading attachments but may not create them" (or withhold a platform service's grant entirely). Before, cloud had to wrap an internal security-service function to get this, and a rename of that function would have silently dropped the protection.
- Why: 18.4 put storage's attachment set (`storage_attachment_member`: read and create on `sys_attachment`) on every member's baseline. Cloud's control plane is cross-tenant and must not let an organization administrator create attachments there.
- Risk and rollback: opt-in only; nothing changes for a host that does not declare the option. Rollback is a revert.
- Read first: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-baseline-sets.ts` (`readPlatformBaselineOverridesOption`, `applyOverrides`, `unmatchedOverrides`).
- Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run src/platform-baseline-sets`.
- Needed from you: nothing.

## What changes

- `SecurityPluginOptions.platformBaselineOverrides` (new): contributed set name → object → `'read'` (keep read, withhold create) or `'decline'` (withhold the object). Example: `{ storage_attachment_member: { sys_attachment: 'read' } }`. A malformed declaration (non-object, empty set name, a set entry naming no object, object `'*'`, a verdict other than `'read'`/`'decline'`) is refused when the plugin is constructed.
- `platform-baseline-sets.ts`:
  - `PlatformBaselineSets` takes the overrides. In `contribute`, the contribution is first held to every existing seam rule as the contributor wrote it, and only then narrowed. An override never adds a bit: `'read'` on an object the set grants create only withholds that object.
  - The narrowed body is what is registered in the catalog and joined to the baseline, so the data plane, `security/explain`, the effective-access read and the `everyone` anchor all read it.
  - A set the overrides leave granting nothing is not registered, so it holds no name in the engine registry, and joins no baseline (`joined: false`, the answer a no-baseline deployment already gives).
  - `unmatchedOverrides()` lists entries no admitted contribution matched.
- `security-plugin.ts`: at `kernel:bootstrapped`, each unmatched override is logged at `warn`, naming it, so a renamed set or object is said rather than silently left in force.
- `security-plugin-security-service.ts`: the admission line appends what the host narrowed, and its meta carries `overridden`. Without overrides the line is byte-identical to today's (the existing integration pin still passes unchanged).
- `index.ts`: exports the `PlatformBaselineOverride` / `PlatformBaselineOverrides` types for hosts.
- `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`: documents the option under "Who holds the object grant".
- Changeset: `@objectstack/plugin-security` patch, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (review#3 M1).

## Tests

- `platform-baseline-sets.test.ts` (unit): `'read'` narrows and the narrowed body is registered; `'decline'` on one of two objects keeps the other; a fully declined set is not registered and joins nothing; `'read'` never adds read; a contribution the seam refuses is still refused with an override present; unmatched overrides are reported; no override leaves the contribution as is; five malformed declarations refused.
- `platform-baseline-sets.integration.test.ts` (real kernel, card acceptance): with `{ pbs_notes_member: { pbs_note: 'read' } }`, the set still joins, a member reads the object, a member's create is refused 403 and `explain` says create is not allowed, the catalog holds read on / create off, the admission line names the narrowing, and an override naming an uncontributed set is warned once at boot.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run`: 267 files / 6671 tests passed (45 skipped).
- `tsc --noEmit` on `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.test.json`: clean. ESLint on the touched files: clean.

- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.

- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
